rules.title: Review soil moisture and irrigation needs
rules.reason: Soil moisture is lower than usual and is pulling your yield estimate down.
rules.action: Check the moisture in the root zone and consider whether extra irrigation is needed.
rules.source: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56 (Crop Evapotranspiration); ICAR Agronomy Guidelines
limitations: Actual irrigation requirements depend on crop growth stage, soil texture, rooting depth, and localized microclimate.
Model correlation does not guarantee specific yield response to irrigation.

rules.title: Maintain adequate moisture and avoid over-irrigation
rules.reason: Soil moisture is in a good range and is helping your yield estimate.
rules.action: Keep your current watering schedule; avoid extra irrigation, which can cause waterlogging or nutrient loss.
rules.source: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 33 (Yield Response to Water)
limitations: Optimal upper moisture threshold varies between sandy, loamy, and heavy clay soils.
Prolonged saturation can impede soil aeration.

rules.title: Mitigate combined drought and heat moisture stress
rules.reason: Low soil moisture, little rain, and high temperature together mean your field is losing water faster than usual.
rules.action: Check field moisture soon, and consider irrigating or mulching to protect against water loss.
rules.source: WMO / FAO Agricultural Meteorology Compendium; ICAR Drought Management Handbook
limitations: Crop tolerance to combined heat-drought stress is strongly dependent on phenological phase.
Groundwater or canal availability must be verified locally.

rules.title: Inspect field drainage and soil moisture sensor reading
rules.reason: Soil moisture readings are low despite recent heavy rain — this could mean water is running off instead of soaking in, or that the moisture sensor needs checking.
rules.action: Check your field for runoff or soil crusting, and make sure the moisture sensor is placed and calibrated correctly.
limitations: Sandy soils with high percolation rates can drain rapidly within hours of rainfall.
Rainfall data may reflect regional gauges rather than field-level precipitation.

rules.title: Check rice paddy water depth and submergence status
rules.reason: Rice needs a lot of water; your soil moisture reading is below what's recommended for paddy rice.
rules.action: Inspect bund integrity and check the water level in the paddy to protect against water stress during tillering or panicle initiation.
rules.source: ICAR-National Rice Research Institute (NRRI) Production Guidelines; FAO Rice Water Management
limitations: Aerobic or upland rice varieties have lower standing water requirements than conventional lowland cultivars.
Growth stage verification is required before adjusting water levels.

rules.title: Monitor wheat for terminal heat stress
rules.reason: Temperature is higher than ideal for wheat and is lowering your yield estimate.
rules.action: Keep an eye on crop temperature and soil moisture; a light evening watering may help cool the plants if you're able to irrigate.
rules.source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (IIWBR); CIMMYT Wheat Physiology Manual
limitations: Heat sensitivity is highest during anthesis and grain filling; early vegetative stages show greater tolerance.
Do not irrigate during high winds to prevent lodging.

rules.title: Assess maize moisture status during critical growth stages
rules.reason: Maize is very sensitive to water stress, which can seriously hurt pollination and ear development.
rules.action: Check field soil moisture and ensure adequate irrigation, especially if the crop is approaching tasseling or silking.
rules.source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR); FAO Water Management for Maize
limitations: Water stress impact is markedly reduced during early vegetative or late maturity stages.
Verify crop development stage on site.

rules.title: Monitor canopy vigor and conduct field scouting
rules.reason: Your plant greenness reading is lower than average, which is pulling your yield estimate down.
rules.action: Walk the field to check plant greenness, how evenly the crop is growing, and look for pests, disease, or other stress.
rules.source: NASA Earth Observatory Remote Sensing Indices Guide; USDA Agricultural Research Service
limitations: NDVI alone cannot diagnose specific diseases, pests, or nutrient deficiencies.
Young crops naturally exhibit low NDVI during early canopy development.

rules.title: Healthy canopy greenness supporting yield potential
rules.reason: Your plants are showing strong, healthy greenness, which is helping your yield estimate.
rules.action: Keep up your current farming practices, and continue watching the crop through to harvest.
rules.source: USDA ARS Remote Sensing in Agriculture Bulletin
limitations: Dense canopies may saturate NDVI readings above 0.75.
High vegetative growth does not guarantee optimal harvest index.

rules.title: Monitor canopy water status using NDWI trend
rules.reason: Your plant water reading is lower than usual, suggesting the crop may be short on water.
rules.action: Watch the crop for wilting or curling leaves, and check this against your root-zone moisture reading.
rules.source: Gao, B.C. (1996) Remote Sensing of Environment (NDWI Index Specification)
limitations: NDWI is sensitive to soil reflectance in sparse canopies.
Does not replace in-situ soil moisture measurements.

rules.title: Consider standard soil fertility testing
rules.reason: Your yield estimate is well below what's typical for this crop.
rules.action: Consider a standard soil lab test (pH, salinity, organic matter, and nutrients) before your next planting to rule out nutrient problems.
limitations: Yield deficit can arise from weather, water, or management factors unrelated to soil fertility.
CropIQ does not prescribe specific chemical or fertilizer application amounts.

rules.title: Monitor declining soil moisture trend across observations
rules.reason: Soil moisture has dropped more than 20% below what's typical for this field recently — a sign it's drying out.
rules.action: Monitor the field water balance over the coming days and check if organic mulching could help conserve moisture.
limitations: Field expanding mean combines multiple observation points which may encompass differing weather conditions.

rules.title: Monitor crop conditions during elevated ambient temperature
rules.reason: Temperature is high (over 35°C), which can make your crop lose water faster and become heat-stressed.
rules.action: Watch your crop for heat scorch and keep an eye on how quickly soil moisture is dropping.
rules.source: FAO Guidelines on Heat Stress in Agricultural Production
limitations: Ambient air temperature cannot be directly altered by field operations.
Tolerance varies substantially across crop species and varieties.

rules.title: Contextual note on dry weather conditions
rules.reason: Very little rain recently is lowering your yield estimate.
rules.action: Expect dry conditions to continue; focus on conserving soil moisture and keep monitoring the field.
limitations: Precipitation is an external environmental variable and cannot be controlled.
Rainfall measurements may represent point observations.

rules.title: High yield risk alert: Prioritize investigation of key downward drivers
rules.reason: Overall, this plot is at high risk — several conditions are combining to pull your yield estimate down.
rules.action: Check the conditions flagged above by walking the field yourself to confirm what's happening on the ground.
limitations: Risk score reflects model-estimated risk based on available inputs, not a guaranteed field loss.
External factors not captured in the dataset (pests, hail, salinity) are not represented.

rules.title: Moderate yield risk alert: Review key downward factors
rules.reason: This plot is at moderate risk — worth keeping an eye on.
rules.action: Look at what's holding your yield back and keep monitoring so it doesn't get worse.
limitations: Moderate risk reflects balanced or slightly depressed yield signals relative to historical benchmarks.

rules.title: High model uncertainty: Verify field conditions before major decisions
rules.reason: CropIQ is less confident than usual about this estimate for your specific mix of conditions.
rules.action: Treat this estimate as a rough guide, and check actual field conditions yourself before making any costly or hard-to-reverse decisions.
limitations: Uncertainty reflects model tree variance, not field variability.

rules.title: Data quality alert: Inputs fall outside typical model training bounds
rules.reason: One or more of the values you entered are outside the range CropIQ usually sees, so it's estimating beyond what it has learned from.
rules.action: Double-check the numbers you entered and your sensor readings to make sure they're accurate.
limitations: Out-of-distribution inputs reduce prediction reliability but do not inherently mean the crop is failing.

rules.title: Verify flagged data values to improve estimate reliability
rules.reason: Some of the data used for this estimate was missing, filled in automatically, or looked unusual.
rules.action: Double-check the flagged values against what you actually observe on your farm for the most accurate estimate.
limitations: Missing features were imputed using training set medians.
